title: The Answering Bullet
dek: On the assassination of Charlie Kirk
subject: The assassination of Charlie Kirk
voice_note: Written in the voice of Thomas Carlyle (1795–1881), through the writer-carlyle skill. An emulation — the prose and judgments are not the historical Carlyle’s own words.
body:
It is done: in the bright forenoon, under a white canopy pitched on the green of a Utah university, a young man sits answering the questions of all comers; and across the autumn air there travels one rifle-shot, and the answerer answers no more. Orem, in the State of Utah; the tenth day of September, 2025. One-and-thirty years he had lived. Behold him fallen sideways in his chair, the microphone yet warm, the half-finished sentence hanging unfinished forever in the bright American air.

Who was he, this Charles Kirk? A Talker; let us not pretend otherwise. A Stump-Orator of the new sort, microphoned and multiplied, who had made of perpetual Speech a vocation and an industry; whose vocables went out by the million into every idle ear of a distracted continent; whom this writer, had he met him living, would assuredly have scolded for the noise of him. The Age of Vocables found in him one of its loudest sons.

And yet,— mark it well, O reader, for here is the one Reality in the matter,— this man did a thing the common Stump-Orator never dares. He pitched his table in the open field; he wrote upon it *Prove Me Wrong*; he sat down unarmed amid the young and the hostile and said, in effect: Here am I; contradict me to my face. Whatsoever the worth of his doctrines, and much of it was light enough, that posture was not Cant. It was the old sacred contest of the Word answered by the Word,— the one human method by which Chaos is ever beaten back a little toward Cosmos. He invited the answering tongue.

They sent him, instead, the answering bullet.

And that, my friends, is the whole tragedy, and the whole judgment, in a single stroke. For consider what an assassin is. He is the man who, having no Word wherewith to answer, reaches for the rifle; who confesses, in the very act, that argument has died in him, that he cannot out-speak his adversary and has resolved therefore to out-shoot him. The marksman on the rooftop is not the opposite of the Stump-Orator,— he is the Stump-Orator's last and lowest avatar, Cant grown so hollow that it has given up even on speech. He has nothing to say; and so he says it with lead.

Woe, then, to the Age that breeds him! A People that will settle the contest of tongues by the crack of a sharpshooter has pronounced sentence upon itself. It has declared the Word bankrupt and enthroned the Bullet in its room; it has chosen for its arbiter not the Reason that persuades but the Powder that explodes. Lying is not permitted in this Universe; and neither is this: no Republic can long endure that murders its talkers because it has ceased to be able to answer them. The thing is a powder-mine. One spark struck in Utah,— and who shall say where the conflagration stops?

Man, by the nature of him, is definable as an incarnated Word. They shot the Word in the throat, and fancied they had won.

They had not. Turn now, one moment, from the noise to the silence; from the Cause to the man. One-and-thirty years; a wife; little children who will grow into knowledge of their father by the recording of his voice and the manner of his death. There are tears due to him, as to all men; the Maker did not fashion that creature to be felled like an ox in a field among his fellows. Let the partisans bay on either flank; over the body itself a decent humanity may stand bareheaded a moment, and be still.

But the prophecy I will not soften. Hear it, America: the bullet has silenced one questioner and multiplied his question a thousand-fold. The dead man asked, *Prove me wrong;* and his murderer has proved nothing whatever, except that he himself was the deader of the two long before ever the trigger moved. The assassin has gone down among the Phantasms; the question stands yet upon the open table, in the bright air, unanswered and unanswerable by powder.

Light; or, failing that, lightning. Thou hast fired upon the light. Stand ready, then, foolish and unhappy Land, for the lightning.
